title: Polynomial mixing of critical three-dimensional Ising dynamics
formal:
For the zero-field nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on the three-dimensional box \(V_L=\{1,\ldots,L\}^{3}\) with free boundary conditions, at the infinite-lattice critical inverse temperature \(\beta_c(\mathbb Z^3)\) defined below, is the worst-initial-state total-variation mixing time of random-site heat-bath dynamics polynomial in \(L\)? Precisely, do there exist constants \(C,a>0\) such that
\[\forall L\in\mathbb N,\ L\ge1,\qquad t_{\mathrm{mix}}(L,1/4)\le C(L+1)^a?\]
Time is counted in individual site-update attempts. The critical parameter is fixed independently of \(L\), and the target is the exact critical point, not a subcritical parameter approaching it at an unspecified rate.
why: This is a basic question about whether a standard local sampling dynamics remains efficient at a phase transition in three dimensions. The equilibrium system has correlations on many scales, so high-temperature mixing guarantees do not directly apply. A polynomial bound or a superpolynomial obstruction would clarify the computational cost of critical fluctuations in one of the central lattice models.

progress.text: The source records polynomial critical mixing in two dimensions as an earlier established result; it does not extend that theorem to three dimensions.
The published Bauerschmidt–Dagallier result obtains polynomial critical control on free-boundary boxes in dimensions at least five, using the mean-field susceptibility bound.
Prodromidis and Sly prove polynomial mixing at the infinite-regular-tree uniqueness threshold. The parameter in their theorem is distinguished from the cubic-lattice critical point.

status_note: The full November 2022 Bauerschmidt–Dagallier manuscript (published in 2024) and the November 2024 Prodromidis–Sly note were read on 2026-09-14. A bounded later search through 2026 found no polynomial mixing proof or superpolynomial obstruction for the exact critical three-dimensional free-boundary model. Higher-dimensional, tree-threshold and different-initialization results do not resolve this target.

sentences: This question concerns local heat-bath sampling of the Ising model at the critical point of the infinite cubic lattice.
The finite system is a three-dimensional box with free boundaries and zero external field.
It asks whether every initial spin configuration becomes close to equilibrium after polynomially many individual updates.
The critical inverse temperature is specified by the infinite-volume magnetization threshold, without relying on a numerical estimate.
Known critical results in other dimensions and at the regular-tree threshold do not settle this three-dimensional lattice problem.

definitions:
Let \(E_L\) contain each unordered pair of vertices of \(V_L\) at lattice distance \(\|u-v\|_1=\sum_{i=1}^{3}|u_i-v_i|=1\), once. A configuration is \(\sigma\in\Omega_L=\{-1,+1\}^{V_L}\). At inverse temperature \(\beta\ge0\), the Gibbs probability is
\[\pi_{L,\beta}(\sigma)=Z_{L,\beta}^{-1}\exp\!\left(\beta\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E_L}\sigma_u\sigma_v\right),\]
where \(Z_{L,\beta}\) is the sum of the displayed weight over all configurations. Each interaction strength is one, there is no external magnetic field, and free boundary means there are no interactions with vertices outside \(V_L\). Boundary vertices inside the box are updated just like other vertices.

To specify the critical inverse temperature without a numerical approximation, let \(B_R=\{-R,\ldots,R\}^{3}\subset\mathbb Z^3\), for integers \(R\ge1\). Define \(\mu^+_{R,\beta}\) on spins in \(B_R\) by fixing all neighboring exterior spins to \(+1\): its weight is proportional to
\[\exp\!\left(\beta\left[\sum_{\substack{\{u,v\}\subset B_R\\\|u-v\|_1=1}}\sigma_u\sigma_v+\sum_{\substack{u\in B_R,\ v\notin B_R\\\|u-v\|_1=1}}\sigma_u\right]\right).\]
Internal unordered edges and crossing edges are each counted once. Set
\[m_+(\beta)=\inf_{R\ge1}\mathbb E_{\mu^+_{R,\beta}}[\sigma_0],\qquad\beta_c(\mathbb Z^3)=\inf\{\beta\ge0:m_+(\beta)>0\}.\]
The monotone limit of finite-volume plus-boundary magnetizations gives this standard infinite-lattice critical value, which is finite and positive. Plus boundaries are used only in defining the infinite-volume threshold; the finite chain being tested has free boundaries.

In one discrete step, choose a vertex \(v\) uniformly from the \(L^3\) sites, independently of previous choices. With \(h_v(\sigma)=\sum_{u:\{u,v\}\in E_L}\sigma_u\), redraw its spin as \(+1\) with probability
\[\frac{\exp(\beta h_v(\sigma))}{\exp(\beta h_v(\sigma))+\exp(-\beta h_v(\sigma))},\]
and as \(-1\) otherwise, leaving all other spins unchanged. Choosing its existing value still counts as one step. Set \(\beta=\beta_c(\mathbb Z^3)\) and denote the resulting transition matrix by \(P_L\). This finite chain is irreducible and aperiodic and has stationary measure \(\pi_L=\pi_{L,\beta_c}\).

For distributions on \(\Omega_L\), \(\operatorname{TV}(\nu,\pi)=\frac12\sum_{\sigma\in\Omega_L}|\nu(\sigma)-\pi(\sigma)|\). Define
\[t_{\mathrm{mix}}(L,1/4)=\min\{t\in\mathbb N_0:\max_{\sigma\in\Omega_L}\operatorname{TV}(P_L^t(\sigma,\cdot),\pi_L)\le1/4\}.\]
The maximum includes every deterministic initial spin configuration. The question concerns this exact mathematical Markov chain; approximating its transition probabilities on finite-precision hardware is not an additional task. Rates in a continuous-time convention with one rate-one clock per site have an extra factor of the volume relative to individual updates; that normalization does not affect polynomial-versus-superpolynomial classification.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the polynomial mixing bound or its negation for this exact model. A positive proof must establish finite constants independent of \(L\), with the critical parameter, free boundaries, update rule, worst initial state and distance threshold specified here. A negative proof must show that no fixed polynomial bounds this sequence of mixing times. Results at a tree threshold, in another lattice dimension, below criticality, with different boundaries or from a restricted initialization do not meet the criterion.

context_blocks.text: Bauerschmidt and Dagallier relate functional inequalities for Ising dynamics to susceptibility bounds. Their critical finite-volume application uses mean-field susceptibility behavior and yields polynomial control on free-boundary lattice boxes in dimensions at least five. The checked result does not establish the needed hypothesis or conclusion in dimension three.

The source also distinguishes the earlier two-dimensional critical theorem from the higher-dimensional argument. Having polynomial mixing in dimension two and in dimensions at least five leaves the three-dimensional target separate; interpolation between dimensions is not a stated theorem.

The 2024 Prodromidis–Sly note proves polynomial mixing at the uniqueness threshold of the infinite regular tree for bounded-degree graphs. At degree six its parameter is \(\operatorname{arctanh}(1/5)\). The word critical in that title refers to the tree threshold, not to the infinite cubic lattice threshold defined in this card.

Boundary conditions materially affect low-temperature dynamics. The source contrasts slow mixing with free boundaries and a different conjecture under all-plus boundaries. Keeping the free-boundary convention is necessary to preserve this card’s specific critical-lattice question.
